about: Every part the bridge installs at boot and holds by name (apps/dashboard/src/bridge/provided.ts, decision 0151), where
it is declared, what it is, and why it is installed and not imported. the-bridge-stays-narrow.test.mjs reads the
declarations in the syntax tree and fails on a part with no row here, and on a row for a part that is gone.
The store holds the frame's own tools: the route gate, moving between pages, the tip and the toast, the shell, a
refresh, and the verbs a page reaches without carrying their code. It never holds a workspace's records: a read's
answer is the seam's (surfaces/surface-values.ts) or the bridge module's that read it (held-reads.ts, who.ts).
Before a new part: a plain import is the first choice, wherever it does not pull a page's code into the code every
page shares or lean the frame on a page. A part earns its row by saying which of those an import would break.
gate     the route gate and the registry's word for a page, asked by the frame before its first draw
tool     a tool of the frame's own, one for the tab: the shell, the tip, the toast, the clock, the tab's memory
courier  verbs a page reaches without carrying their code, which stays in the chunk that owns it
dial     a number the frame is told, which a test turns down

surfaceState.why: The registry's word for a page (real, demo, unknown), which the frame asks in its first render; the frame's pages and the kit read it without importing the registry and every surface it names.

surfaceRetired.why: Where a retired address lands now, asked beside surfaceState by the same first render.

surfaceGate.why: Whether a route's surfaces are in: the frame's hooks ask it during their first render, before any effect, and a page drawn alone in a test draws without it.

surfaceFailed.why: Whether the surface a route draws from failed to read, asked with the gate.

onSurfaceReady.why: Hears a surface's readiness move, for the gate's hooks; the stop is the answer.

routeWaitMs.why: How long a first draw waits for a band beside its page. A number, held so a test and the e2e harness turn it down.

afterTheMoveMs.why: How long a move's reads wait for its motion to end. A number, held so a test turns it down.

refreshSurface.why: A page's Retry: one surface read again through the runner, so its status, its cache and the pill agree. The runner's list of surfaces imports every page; a page cannot import it back.

tip.why: The one tooltip, shown at a control at once. The kit reads it, and the kit imports nothing of the frame.

toast.why: The one toast every page raises. Read where a part draws it, so the kit and the pages do not import the frame.

shell.why: The shell's verbs over the window: moving between pages, the address, sign-out, the status line. The record kit and the pages reach them without importing the bridge's boot.

chrome.why: The chrome's own words and choices: the themes and looks the account menu offers, what the theme button says. Read by the frame, the toast and the record kit, which imports nothing of the bridge's boot.

clock.why: The business's clock: every page says a time by the workspace's zone from the first paint. One for the tab, and a test hands in its own.

tz.why: The zone's words and the list its picker offers, contracts' own functions, handed to Settings' Business pane beside the workspace's verbs. A candidate for a plain import.

tabMemory.why: The tab's memory of a page's place and its half-done work, over the tab's storage and kept by workspace. Read by the record kit, which imports nothing of the bridge's boot.

bell.why: The bell: its rows as this device sees them, its number, and who hears it. Each is worked out as it is asked from the notices the bridge holds (held-reads.ts); the part holds no rows.

roles.why: Who is acting and what they may do: every gate asks it from the first draw. It reads who is looking (who.ts) as it is asked and holds no list of its own; a test hands in a role.

workspace.why: The active workspace's own change, owner-only: its zone and what it calls a booking. Settings' Business pane reaches it; it reads who is looking (who.ts) as it is asked and holds nothing.

policy.why: The autonomy modes as a chip asks for one. It reads the settings surface as it is asked and holds no rows; every page reaches it through the frame's verbs, and a test hands in a charter.

phoneDoor.why: The phone app's door at sign-out (forget this phone). Installed only inside the app, so the shell asks for it by name.

href.why: A link the browser follows instead of a request it makes (a download, a photo), to one of the app's own routes with the workspace named as the client names it. Reached through the frame's verbs.

setPolicy.why: A mode set from a chip: the policy store calls the save by this name, so a test stands one in for it.

saveSettings.why: The settings save as the Business pane sends it; reached by name so the pane does not carry the bridge's save, and a test stands one in.

replies.why: The verbs over a lead's replies, reached from a thread's strip. The replies themselves are a read the bridge holds (held-reads.ts), not this part.

warmPerson.why: Read someone before their row is pressed, and their page's code with them. People's code stays out of the pages that only reach a person.

personNotes.why: A person's notes, from a thread or Today's row that names them: the sheet's rules stay in People's chunk (the loadability review, 19 Oct 2026).

deal.why: The deal menu's verbs, from a thread that draws a deal: its rules stay in People's chunk.

sheets.why: People's sheets and the asks that open them, which the frame draws and other pages ask for; handed over so the frame does not lean on People.

peopleScopes.why: People's scopes and their routes, the strip's order, for the frame's strip; handed over so the frame does not lean on People.

refreshPlaybooks.why: The playbooks read again after a run's verb on another page; Campaigns' read stays in Campaigns' chunk.

broadcasts.why: Sent's verbs, reached from a run's acts on another page without carrying Campaigns' code.

calendar.why: The Calendar's verbs, reached from Settings' Business pane without carrying the Calendar's code.

billing.why: Billing's verbs (its view model, the way to checkout), reached from the shell's band without carrying Settings' billing code.
